screening_decisions.reason: This is a randomised multicentre trial evaluating adjuvant medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) in patients with stage I endometrial carcinoma after surgery. Patients were randomised to MPA vs no treatment or radiotherapy vs radiotherapy plus MPA. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a literature review/survey, not a randomised controlled trial. The abstract states 'A survey of the literature shows...' and discusses findings from multiple studies rather than presenting original RCT data.

This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis techniques, not a clinical trial. The abstract is truncated but the title indicates it is about statistical methodology for measuring inconsistency in meta-analyses.
This is a methodological chapter about statistical methods for meta-analysis, not a clinical trial. The abstract describes formulae and methods for combining trial results.

This is a randomized controlled trial of adjuvant progestagen therapy (progesterone) in patients with Stage I or II endometrial cancer after surgery. 1148 patients were randomly assigned to adjuvant progesterone or no additional therapy after surgery.

This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis approaches, not a clinical trial. The abstract discusses random effects approaches to combining evidence from trials, not presenting original trial data.

This is a randomized trial of progestogens in patients with endometrial carcinoma treated with surgery and radiotherapy. 429 patients were randomized to progestogen or control group, and all patients underwent operation. Meets selection criteria as an RCT of progestagen therapy in women who had surgery.

This is a methodological paper about extracting statistics from published literature for meta-analysis, not a clinical trial. The abstract describes methods for extracting log hazard ratios and variance from published studies.

This is a randomized controlled trial of 6-methyl-17α-hydroxyprogesterone (a progestagen) in patients with stage IA or IB endometrial carcinoma after surgery. 35 patients were randomized to hydroxyprogesterone or placebo after total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy.

This is a randomized controlled trial of adjuvant progestagen therapy in endometrial cancer after surgery. 205 patients were randomly assigned to adjuvant progestagen treatment or no additional therapy after surgery.
